title: incident-continuity-briefs-and-simulation-playbook
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Summary
This document provides a continuity-centric incident playbook that pairs technical runbook steps with pre-written stakeholder briefs and game-day simulations. The goal is to shorten time-to-recovery, standardize communications, and ensure consistent debriefs that drive corrective actions.

Scope
- Applies to all customer-facing inference endpoints (hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane) and related routing services.
- Covers detection, triage, containment, mitigation, stakeholder comms, status page updates, and post-incident debrief.
- Does NOT replace product-specific runbooks; treat this as the canonical continuity and comms layer.

Objectives
- Verify impact and classify severity within 10 minutes of first page.
- Contain customer-visible degradation within 30 minutes for Sev1 incidents.
- Produce a blameless postmortem and prioritized action plan within 7 business days.

Incident Severity (triage rules)
- Sev0 (Platform-wide outage): All inference traffic disrupted across regions or control plane unavailable. Immediate incident command (IC) required. Target: restore control-plane reachability or failover within 15 minutes.
- Sev1 (Major degradation): High error rate (>5% user-facing error rate OR p95 latency > 2x target for >50% of requests) for a primary region or global model catalog mismatch. Target: containment within 30 minutes, mitigation within 2 hours.
- Sev2 (Partial impact / single-customer): Isolated customer-facing issues, degraded throughput for a small set of tenants. Target: acknowledge 30 minutes, resolution or workaround within 24 hours.

Roles & Responsibilities
- Pager (Primary oncall): First responder. Run triage checklist, gather logs, follow runbook steps or escalate.
- Incident Lead (IC): Coordinates triage, declares severity, owns comms cadence and status page updates.
- Service Engineer / On-call SME: Executes remediation steps, rollback, or mitigations.
- SRE Platform Lead: If infrastructure-level failure, owns failover and capacity changes.
- Product / PM: Represents product impact and business priorities.
- Customer Success / Support: Prepares customer-level communications and helps prioritize affected tenants.
- Communications Lead (optional): Drafts executive brief and external status updates.

Initial Triage Checklist (first 10 minutes)
1) Acknowledge page and confirm on-call roster.
2) Identify scope: affected regions, models, endpoints, tenants. Use: 
   - observability dashboard: /dashboards/inference-slo
   - kubernetes: kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide
   - routing: curl -sS https://internal-router.healthz
3) Snapshot metrics: error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, healthy host count, GPU utilization.
4) Determine probable domain: code, infra, routing, model, third-party.
5) If severity unknown, default to higher severity and follow IC escalation.

Containment & Mitigation Playbook (generic steps)
- If request errors spike: 1) Disable recent traffic routes/flags via Router Console; 2) Scale up replica sets or shift traffic to Dedicated fallback pool; 3) Apply rate-limiting or circuit-breaker at edge.
- If latency increases but errors are low: 1) Check cache/KV hit rates and KV-read latencies; 2) Inspect model host CPU/GPU saturation; 3) Temporarily reduce max_tokens or force a quantized model variant.
- If model artifact mismatch: 1) Promote previous stable model version (pin in deployment config); 2) Run quick smoke tests: curl -X POST /v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"healthcheck"}'
- If control plane unavailable: 1) Failover to secondary control plane region; 2) Alert account teams for impacted Dedicated/private customers.

Example CLI snippets (safe to paste)
- Retrieve recent container restarts:
  kubectl get pods -n inference -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, restarts: .status.containerStatuses[].restartCount}'
- Smoke test a model endpoint (replace variables):
  curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' \ 
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
    -d '{"input":"healthcheck"}' \ 
    https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/models/$MODEL_ID/generate

Escalation Matrix (contact order / SLA targets)
| Role | Contact | Pager | Target response |
| Incident Lead | @oncall-rotations | pager | 5 minutes |
| Service Owner | service-owner@redwood.com | pager | 10 minutes |
| SRE Platform Lead | sre-platform@redwood.com | pager | 15 minutes |
| Product Lead | product@redwood.com | email | 30 minutes |

(When contacting external vendors, include request_id, timestamps, and metric snapshots.)

Stakeholder Brief Templates
1) Internal SEV1 Brief (10–15 min post-declaration)\Subject: [SEV1] Short summary — Impacted service(s) | Initial action
Body:
- What happened: Short one-line summary.
- When it started: 2026-02-18T14:03Z (UTC)
- Impact: e.g., 40% error-rate on /v1/generate in us-west1; 12% of requests failing with 503
- Current state: Containment in place (traffic diverted to fallback), mitigation ongoing.
- Next steps: (1) scale fallback pools, (2) revert recent config change, (3) update status page in 30 minutes.
- Owner: Incident Lead — Maya Thompson

2) Executive brief (30–60 min)\Subject: Executive update: [SEV1] Service disruption impacting inference API
Body:
- Short summary and customer impact (est. number of tenants affected)
- Business impact and risk (SLAs at risk, revenue-sensitive customers)
- Actions taken and ETA for next update
- Key ask (e.g., pre-approve urgent capacity commit or communication sign-off)

3) External customer status update (Status Page / Email)\Subject: Redwood API: Partial outage affecting inference responses in us-west1
Body:
We are investigating an issue affecting inference responses in us-west1. Some requests may return 503 or experience elevated latency. Our engineering team has applied traffic routing workarounds and mitigation is in progress. We will provide an update by 15:30 UTC or sooner.

Status Page Guidance
- Use three tiers: Investigating, Identified, Mitigated, Resolved.
- Update cadence: every 30 minutes while incident is active, or sooner after critical milestones.
- Include: symptoms, affected tenants/regions, mitigation steps taken, ETA for next update, link to support contact.

On-call Rotation & Handoff
- Structure: Primary (7 days), Secondary (7 days), Backup (monthly), Follow-the-sun coverage via regional pods.
- Recommended handoff checklist (to be run at change of shift):
  - Confirm scheduled maintenance windows and active deploys.
  - Verify the following: current open incidents, outstanding action items, runbook health, scheduled game-days.
  - Run live smoke tests against a list of endpoints and attach results.
  - Update calendar and status slack channel with your coverage window.

Handoff Checklist (template)\\- Name: <outgoing_oncall>\\- Name: <incoming_oncall>\\- Date/Time:
- Open incidents (IDs and brief status)
- Pending deploys that may affect service
- Active mitigations and expected completion times
- Signed-off: outgoing -> incoming

Schedule generator (example)\\- Simple helper (bash) to pick primary/secondary for N engineers:
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  due="$(date +%Y-%m-%d)"
  eng=("alice" "bob" "carol" "dan")
  idx=$(( ( $(date -d "$due" +%s) / 86400 ) % ${#eng[@]} ))
  echo "Primary: ${eng[$idx]}\nSecondary: ${eng[$(( (idx+1) % ${#eng[@]} ))]}"

Game-day Scenarios & Success Criteria
1) Multi-region failover (24–48 hours)\- Scenario: us-west1 control plane loses persistent access.\- Exercise steps: declare IC, fail traffic to us-east1, validate consumer traffic, measure end-to-end latency.\- Success: Failover completed < 20 minutes; no more than 2% of production requests return 5xx during switch.

2) Model rollout regression (2 hours)\- Scenario: New model rollout increases 5xxs for a subset of routes.\- Exercise: Trigger canary assessment, automatically revert canary, run smoke tests against previous model.\- Success: Canary detection triggers rollback < 10 minutes, regression pipeline blocks re-rollout until fix validated.

3) Cache-layer meltdown (1 hour)\- Scenario: KV store cluster experiences slow IO causing high p95 tail latency.\- Exercise steps: Detect via cache-miss spike, switch to degraded cache mode (read-through bypass), and scale KV cluster.\- Success: P95 latency returns to within 1.5x SLO within 30 minutes of mitigation.

Post-incident Debrief & Postmortem Process
- Timeline: Within 48 hours produce an incident timeline draft; within 7 business days publish a blameless postmortem with: impact, timeline, root cause hypothesis, corrective actions, owners and ETA.
- Postmortem template checklist:
  - Title and summary
  - Incident timeline (ISO timestamps)
  - Metrics + graphs (attach links)
  - Root cause analysis (with evidence)
  - Contributing factors and mitigations
  - Action items with owners and due dates
  - Postmortem review attendees

Metrics & Observability to collect during incident
- API error rate (5xx, 4xx) per endpoint and model
- Latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) by region and model
- Host-level CPU/GPU utilization and queue lengths
- Cache hit ratio, KV latency, and circuit breaker tripping rates
- Routing success rate and healthy host counts

Runbook Ownership & Maintenance
- Each runbook must list: owner, last-reviewed date, review cadence (quarterly), and links to related playbooks.
- Label runbooks with stability tags: stable | experimental | deprecated.

FAQ & Common Mistakes
- Q: When should I immediately escalate to SRE Platform Lead?
  A: When the issue involves persistent disk, control plane latency, or region-wide unhealthy host counts that cannot be mitigated by service-level restarts.
- Q: Can we silently rollback a model without notifying Product?
  A: No — always notify Product and the incident owner after rollback.

Appendices
- Template: Short SMS/Slack alert to customers:
  [Redwood] We are investigating increased errors for inference responses in us-west1. Estimated next update in 30 min.
- Template: Full customer email (for resolved incidents)\Subject: Incident resolved: Inference API degraded performance in us-west1\Body:
  We resolved an issue impacting inference responses in us-west1. Root cause: mis-deployed model artifact. Impact: ~12% of requests returned 503 between 14:00–14:28 UTC. Fix: rolled back to prior model and restored routing. Actions: added pre-rollout smoke checks, expanded canary size controls. Customers needing impacted request logs should contact support@redwood-inference.com.

Contact & escalation list
- Pager channel: #oncall-redwood (primary)
- Incident commander email: incident-command@redwood.com
- Support triage: support@redwood-inference.com

Related pages & references

- Runbook library: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks

Document maintenance
- Owner: engineering (Maya Thompson)
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any Sev0/Sev1 incident
- Last reviewed: 2026-02-18
